title: Hosted Call Trial
statement: Let $M_V$, $M_I$, and $M_P$ be Boolean finite-state Turing machines, let $x$ and $u$ be Boolean words, let $b$ be a Boolean value, and let $s$ be a natural number. Suppose the cleaned simulation of $M_V$, started in its initial cleaning state on input $x\mathbin{++}u$, halts with output $b$, leaves all its work tapes blank with their heads at position $0$, and keeps every work-tape head within distance $s$ of $0$ throughout the run. Then the call-phase machine, started with input-head position $1$, the first tape storing $u$, the second storing $x\mathbin{++}u$, and the call simulation in its initial state, reaches a configuration with input-head position $1$, the first two tapes still storing $u$ and $x\mathbin{++}u$, the third tape storing the one-symbol word $[b]$, and its third-tape head at position $1$. It does not enter its designated exit state earlier, and throughout the run every work-tape head has absolute position at most $|x|+|u|+s+1$.
hypotheses_covered: $M_V$, $M_I$, and $M_P$ are Boolean finite-state Turing machines
The cleaned simulation of $M_V$ on $x\mathbin{++}u$ halts with output $b$
At halt, all work tapes of the cleaned simulation are blank and all heads are at $0$
Throughout the cleaned simulation, every work-tape head has absolute position at most $s$
